title: Chapter, Verse & Cover Letter
description: A challenging round mixing harder Bible trivia from wisdom literature and the epistles, classic novels and their opening lines, career knowledge, and the stage and page.

questions.question: Spanning 150 chapters, this longest book of the Bible was Israel's ancient hymnal and prayer guide — with chapter 23 its most beloved passage.
This book's central character is a blameless man stripped of health and wealth by Satan's wager with God — and fully restored twofold at the end.
'Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding' is one of the most quoted lines from this book, credited largely to Solomon.
Its repeated opening cry 'Vanity of vanities! All is vanity' sets the tone for this Old Testament book's reflections on the emptiness of earthly pursuits.
This 7-chapter minor prophet contains the famous line 'What does the Lord require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.' (6:8)
Acts 2 describes this event — 50 days after Passover — when the Holy Spirit descended as tongues of fire and the disciples spoke in languages they had never learned.
Written from prison, this Pauline letter contains 'I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me' and the command to 'rejoice in the Lord always.'
Paul's most systematic theological letter builds to the declaration 'There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.'
After Paul and Silas were jailed in this Macedonian city, an earthquake opened the cell doors — and their terrified jailer asked, 'What must I do to be saved?'
This anonymous New Testament letter argues Christ is superior to Moses, the angels, and the Levitical priesthood — and its Chapter 11 is a 'hall of faith' roll call of Abel, Enoch, Noah, and Abraham.
Charles Dickens set this novel during the French Revolution, opening with 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times,' and following the selfless Sydney Carton to the guillotine.
questions.answer: What is A Tale of Two Cities?

questions.question: In this George Orwell novel, the Party of Oceania enforces 'doublethink,' 'thoughtcrime,' and the slogan 'War is peace, freedom is slavery, ignorance is strength.'
F. Scott Fitzgerald's Jazz Age masterpiece follows the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby's obsessive love for Daisy Buchanan across Long Island Sound.
John Steinbeck won the 1940 Pulitzer Prize for this novel following the Joad family as they flee Dust Bowl Oklahoma along Route 66 toward California.
questions.answer: What is The Grapes of Wrath?

questions.question: Franz Kafka's 1915 novella opens with traveling salesman Gregor Samsa waking to discover he has been transformed into a giant insect.
'Call me Ishmael' opens this 1851 Herman Melville novel about Captain Ahab's obsessive hunt for a great white whale.
'It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife' opens this Jane Austen classic.
'Last night I dreamt I went to Manderley again' opens this 1938 gothic novel, in which an unnamed narrator marries a wealthy widower haunted by the memory of his first wife.
J.R.R. Tolkien's 1937 adventure about the reluctant Bilbo Baggins begins with a sentence describing a creature living in an underground dwelling.
'Whether I shall turn out to be the hero of my own life, or whether that station will be held by anybody else, these pages must show' opens this Dickens novel about a poor orphan's rise.
This one-to-two-page document summarizes a job seeker's work history, education, and skills for a hiring manager, typically in reverse chronological order.
Sent alongside your application, this document lets you explain in your own voice why you want a specific role and what makes you uniquely qualified.
Title VII of this landmark 1964 U.S. law prohibits employers from discriminating on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin — reshaping the American workplace.
questions.answer: What is the Civil Rights Act?

questions.question: This structured interview technique — prompted by 'Tell me about a time when…' — asks candidates to describe a Situation, Task, Action, and Result, forming its four-letter acronym.

This 1969 management concept — named after its Canadian-American author — holds that employees in a hierarchy are promoted until they reach a role that exceeds their competence, where they remain stuck.
This Shakespeare tragedy follows a Scottish general who murders King Duncan to seize the throne, only to be destroyed by guilt, prophecy, and Macduff's sword.
Edgar Allan Poe's most famous poem features a tormented narrator and a mysterious bird that responds to every question with a single haunting word.
This Shakespeare comedy ends in a fairy-enchanted forest where the sprite Puck delivers the sardonic line 'Lord, what fools these mortals be!'
questions.answer: What is A Midsummer Night's Dream?

questions.question: Walt Whitman's sprawling 1855 poem — the centerpiece of 'Leaves of Grass' — celebrates the self, the body, democracy, and the American experience across 52 sections.
Arthur Miller's 1949 play — which won both the Pulitzer Prize and the Tony Award — follows traveling salesman Willy Loman as he confronts his failures and the collapse of his American Dream.
questions.answer: What is Death of a Salesman?
